553:         } catch {
554:           this.addLog(targetId, 'system', `⚠️ Không tìm thấy script: ${inst.profile.script} (trong scripts/) - bỏ qua script`);
555:         }
556:       }
557: 
558:       inst.mccProcess = spawn(this.binaryPath, args, {
559:         cwd: process.cwd(),
560:         env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'xterm-256color' },
561:       });
562: 
563:       inst.startTime = Date.now();
564:       this.broadcastStatus(targetId);
565: 
566:       if (inst.mccProcess.stdout) {
567:         inst.mccProcess.stdout.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
568:           const raw = chunk.toString('utf-8');
569:           const lines = raw.split(/\r?\n/);
570:           for (const line of lines) {
571:             if (!line.trim()) continue;
572:             const cleanText = line.replace(/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]/g, '').trim();
573:             this.addLog(targetId, 'mcc', cleanText, line);
574:             this.parseAndBroadcastCoords(targetId, cleanText);
575:           }
576:         });
577:       }
578: 
579:       if (inst.mccProcess.stderr) {
580:         inst.mccProcess.stderr.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
581:           const line = chunk.toString('utf-8').trim();
582:           if (line) {
583:             this.addLog(targetId, 'error', `[stderr] ${line}`, line);
584:           }
585:         });
586:       }
587: 
588:       inst.mccProcess.on('exit', (code, signal) => {
589:         const uptimeMs = inst.startTime ? Date.now() - inst.startTime : 0;
590:         this.addLog(targetId, 'kicked', `[MCC Process Exited] Exit Code: ${code ?? 'N/A'}, Signal: ${signal ?? 'N/A'}, Uptime: ${Math.floor(uptimeMs / 1000)}s`);
591:         inst.mccProcess = null;
592:         inst.startTime = 0;
593:         this.broadcastStatus(targetId);
594: 
595:         // Auto-relaunch when the server drops the connection during login
596:         // (AquaMC rate-limits logins per IP -> EndOfStreamException / "logging in too fast").
597:         // Only retry quick exits (< 30s), with backoff, and not when the user stopped it.
598:         if (
599:           !inst.stoppedByUser &&
600:           uptimeMs < QUICK_EXIT_THRESHOLD_MS &&
601:           inst.retryCount < RELAUNCH_BACKOFFS.length
602:         ) {
603:           const delayMs = RELAUNCH_BACKOFFS[inst.retryCount];
604:           inst.retryCount += 1;
605:           this.addLog(
606:             targetId,
607:             'system',
608:             `🔄 Server đã drop kết nối khi login (rate-limit/EOF). Tự động kết nối lại lần ${inst.retryCount}/${RELAUNCH_BACKOFFS.length} sau ${Math.round(delayMs / 1000)}s...`
609:           );
610:           inst.retryTimer = setTimeout(() => {
611:             inst.retryTimer = null;
612:             this.startMCC(targetId, true);
613:           }, delayMs);
614:         } else if (!inst.stoppedByUser) {
615:           inst.retryCount = 0;
616:         }
617:       });
618: 
619:       inst.mccProcess.on('error', (err) => {
620:         this.addLog(targetId, 'error', `[MCC Process Error] ${err.message}`);
621:         inst.mccProcess = null;
622:         inst.startTime = 0;
623:         this.broadcastStatus(targetId);
624:       });
625:     } catch (err: any) {
626:       this.addLog(targetId, 'error', `Failed to start MCC process: ${err.message}`);
627:     }
628:   }

630:   public async stopMCC(accountId?: string): Promise<void> {
631:     const targetId = accountId || this.activeAccountId;
632:     const inst = this.instances.get(targetId);
633:     if (!inst || !inst.mccProcess || inst.mccProcess.killed) {
634:       if (inst) inst.mccProcess = null;
635:       this.addLog(targetId, 'system', `[MCC Manager] No active process to stop for account ${targetId}.`);
636:       return;
637:     }
638: 
639:     this.addLog(targetId, 'system', `⏹️ Stopping Minecraft Console Client for account ${inst.profile.name}...`);
640:     inst.stoppedByUser = true;
641:     if (inst.retryTimer) {
642:       clearTimeout(inst.retryTimer);
643:       inst.retryTimer = null;
644:     }
645: 
646:     return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
647:       let resolved = false;
648:       const cleanupAndResolve = () => {
649:         if (!resolved) {
650:           resolved = true;
651:           inst.mccProcess = null;
652:           inst.startTime = 0;
653:           this.broadcastStatus(targetId);
654:           resolve();
655:         }
656:       };
657: 
658:       const proc = inst.mccProcess;
659:       if (!proc) return cleanupAndResolve();
660: 
661:       proc.once('exit', cleanupAndResolve);
662:       proc.once('close', cleanupAndResolve);
663: 
664:       try {
665:         if (proc.stdin && !proc.stdin.destroyed) {
666:           proc.stdin.write('/quit\n');
667:         }
668:       } catch (e) {}
669: 
670:       setTimeout(() => {
671:         try {
672:           if (proc && !proc.killed) {
673:             proc.kill('SIGKILL');
674:           }
675:         } catch (e) {}
676:         cleanupAndResolve();
677:       }, 1500);
678:     });
679:   }

688:   /**
689:    * Stop MCC (if running), wait for its on-exit INI rewrite, then write our INI
690:    * content and start MCC again. MCC rewrites bot.ini from its in-memory config
691:    * when it exits, so writing the INI before the stop gets clobbered.
692:    */
693:   private async stopThenSaveIniAndRestart(targetId: string, raw: string) {
694:     const inst = this.instances.get(targetId);
695:     const wasRunning = inst && inst.mccProcess && !inst.mccProcess.killed;
696:     if (wasRunning) {
697:       this.addLog(targetId, 'system', '⏳ Khởi động lại MCC để áp dụng cài đặt mới...');
698:       await this.stopMCC(targetId);
699:       await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500));
700:     }
701:     await this.saveIniContent(raw, targetId);
702:     if (wasRunning) {
703:       await this.startMCC(targetId);
704:     }
705:   }

1026:   public handleClientMessage(ws: WebSocket, msg: WSMessageFromClient) {
1027:     const currentState = this.clientState.get(ws);
1028:     const clientActiveId = currentState?.activeAccountId || this.activeAccountId;
1029:     const targetAccountId = msg.type === 'SELECT_ACCOUNT' ? msg.accountId : (msg as any).accountId || clientActiveId;
1030: 
1031:     switch (msg.type) {
1032:       case 'SELECT_ACCOUNT':
1033:         this.selectAccountForClient(ws, msg.accountId);
1034:         break;
1035:       case 'ADD_ACCOUNT':
1036:         this.addAccount(msg.profile).then((newId) => {
1037:           this.selectAccountForClient(ws, newId);
1038:         });
1039:         break;
1040:       case 'UPDATE_ACCOUNT':
1041:         if (msg.profile.serverHost && msg.profile.username) {
1042:           this.updateServerAccount(
1043:             msg.profile.serverHost,
1044:             msg.profile.serverPort || 25565,
1045:             msg.profile.username,
1046:             msg.profile.password,
1047:             msg.profile.accountType || 'mojang',
1048:             msg.profile.method || 'mcc',
1049:             msg.profile.minecraftVersion,
1050:             msg.accountId
1051:           );
1052:           // Update script if provided
1053:           if (msg.profile.script !== undefined) {
1054:             const targetId = msg.accountId || clientActiveId;
1055:             const inst = this.instances.get(targetId);
1056:             if (inst) {
1057:               inst.profile.script = msg.profile.script || undefined;
1058:               this.saveAccountsToDisk(Array.from(this.instances.values()).map((i) => i.profile));
1059:               this.generateRunSh(inst);
1060:               this.broadcastAccountsList();
1061:             }
1062:           }
1063:         }
1064:         break;
1065:       case 'DELETE_ACCOUNT':
1066:         this.deleteAccount(msg.accountId);
1067:         break;
1068:       case 'START_MCC':
1069:         this.startMCC(targetAccountId);
1070:         break;
1071:       case 'STOP_MCC':
1072:         this.stopMCC(targetAccountId);
1073:         break;
1074:       case 'RESTART_MCC':
1075:         this.restartMCC(targetAccountId);
1076:         break;
1077:       case 'SEND_COMMAND':
1078:       case 'SEND_CHAT':
1079:         this.sendCommand(msg.type === 'SEND_COMMAND' ? msg.command : msg.message, targetAccountId);
1080:         break;
1081:       case 'GET_INI':
1082:         this.sendIniContentToClient(ws, targetAccountId);
1083:         break;
1084:       case 'SAVE_INI':

305:   const escapeBackslashes = (quoted: string): string => {
306:     if (!quoted.includes('\\')) return quoted;
307:     const quoteChar = quoted[0];
308:     const inner = quoted.slice(1, -1);
309:     const escaped = inner.replace(/\\(?!\\)/g, '\\\\');
310:     return quoteChar + escaped + quoteChar;
311:   };

313:   for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
314:     let line = lines[i];
315:     const trimmed = line.trim();

317:     // Skip empty lines or pure comment lines
318:     if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('#') || trimmed.startsWith(';')) {
319:       repairedLines.push(line);
320:       continue;
321:     }

323:     // 1. Fix Section Headers e.g. [ChatBot.AutoRespond (missing ']') or [ChatBot.AutoRespond.]
324:     if (trimmed.startsWith('[')) {
325:       // Check if missing closing bracket
326:       if (!trimmed.includes(']')) {
327:         let name = trimmed.replace(/^\[+/, '').trim();
328:         name = name.replace(/\.+$|^\.+/g, ''); // strip trailing or leading dots
329:         line = `[${name}]`;
330:         fixCount++;
331:         logs.push(`Dòng ${i + 1}: Thêm dấu ']' còn thiếu cho section header -> [${name}]`);
332:       } else {
333:         // Has both brackets, clean up extra dots inside or outside e.g. [ChatBot.AutoRespond.]
334:         const match = line.match(/^(\s*)\[+([^\]]+)\]+(\s*)$/);
335:         if (match) {
336:           const indent = match[1];
337:           let secName = match[2].trim();
338:           const cleanName = secName.replace(/^\.+|\.+$|(?<=\.)\.+/g, ''); // remove leading/trailing or double dots
339:           if (secName !== cleanName) {
340:             line = `${indent}[${cleanName}]`;
341:             fixCount++;
342:             logs.push(`Dòng ${i + 1}: Sửa tên section header -> [${cleanName}]`);

344:         }
345:       }
346:       repairedLines.push(line);
347:       continue;
348:     }

350:     // 2. Fix Inline Object Syntax e.g. Server = { Host = 127.0.0.1, Port = 25565 } or Account = { Login = geasf }

355:         const key = kvMatch[2].trim();
356:         const inner = kvMatch[3];
357:         const comment = kvMatch[4] || '';
358: 
359:         // Process inner properties e.g. Host = 127.0.0.1, Port = 25565
360:         const props = inner.split(',').map((p) => p.trim()).filter(Boolean);
361:         let innerModified = false;
362: 
363:         const fixedProps = props.map((prop) => {
364:           const propMatch = prop.match(/^([a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+)\s*=\s*(.*)$/);
365:           if (propMatch) {
366:             const pKey = propMatch[1].trim();
367:             let pVal = propMatch[2].trim();
368: 
369:             // Unquote erroneously quoted empty array strings e.g. Times = "[ ]"
370:             if (pVal === '"[ ]"' || pVal === "'[ ]'") {
371:               pVal = '[ ]';
372:               innerModified = true;
373:             } else if (
374:               !pVal.startsWith('"') &&
375:               !pVal.startsWith("'") &&
376:               !pVal.startsWith('[') &&
377:               pVal.toLowerCase() !== 'true' &&
378:               pVal.toLowerCase() !== 'false' &&
379:               isNaN(Number(pVal))
380:             ) {
381:               pVal = `"${pVal}"`;
382:               innerModified = true;
383:             }
384: 
385:             // Escape unescaped backslashes in quoted values (fixes "\\. invalid escape sequence")
386:             if (pVal.startsWith('"') && pVal.includes('\\')) {
387:               const safeVal = escapeBackslashes(pVal);
388:               if (safeVal !== pVal) {
389:                 pVal = safeVal;
390:                 innerModified = true;
391:               }
392:             }
393:             return `${pKey} = ${pVal}`;
394:           }
395:           return prop;
396:         });
397: 
398:         if (innerModified) {
399:           line = `${indent}${key} = { ${fixedProps.join(', ')} }${comment}`;
400:           fixCount++;
401:           logs.push(`Dòng ${i + 1}: Sửa dấu ngoặc kép cho đối tượng ${key} -> { ${fixedProps.join(', ')} }`);
402:         }
403:       }
404:       repairedLines.push(line);
405:       continue;
406:     }
407: 
408:     // 3. Fix Unquoted Strings or TOML Array Keys e.g. ChatBot, Matches_File = matches.ini, ServerIP = 127.0.0.1
409:     const kvMatch = line.match(/^(\s*)([a-zA-Z0-9_\-.]+)\s*=\s*(.*)$/);
410:     if (kvMatch) {
411:       const indent = kvMatch[1];
412:       const key = kvMatch[2].trim();
413:       let valAndComment = kvMatch[3].trim();
414: 
415:       // Separate inline comment
416:       let val = valAndComment;
417:       let comment = '';
418:       const hashIdx = valAndComment.indexOf('#');
419:       const semiIdx = valAndComment.indexOf(';');
420:       const commentIdx = hashIdx !== -1 && semiIdx !== -1 ? Math.min(hashIdx, semiIdx) : (hashIdx !== -1 ? hashIdx : semiIdx);

422:       if (commentIdx !== -1) {

424:         comment = ' ' + valAndComment.slice(commentIdx).trim();
425:       }
426: 
427:       // Check if key is a known TOML Array property (e.g. ChatBot, Bots, BotOwners, Matches, Excludes)
428:       const ARRAY_KEYS = ['chatbot', 'bots', 'botowners', 'matches', 'excludes', 'packetdebugexclusions', 'entites_list', 'script', 'commands'];
429:       const isArrayKey = ARRAY_KEYS.includes(key.toLowerCase());
430: 
431:       if (isArrayKey) {
432:         // If it's already formatted as a TOML array e.g. [ "AutoRespond" ], do not touch
433:         if (val.startsWith('[') && val.endsWith(']')) {
434:           repairedLines.push(line);
435:           continue;
436:         }
437: 
438:         // Format unquoted list/string into a TOML Array e.g. ChatBot = [ "AutoRespond" ]
439:         const items = val
440:           .split(',')
441:           .map((s) => s.trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, ''))
442:           .filter(Boolean);
443: 
444:         const newArrVal = items.length > 0 ? `[ ${items.map((it) => `"${it}"`).join(', ')} ]` : '[ ]';
445:         line = `${indent}${key} = ${newArrVal}${comment}`;

447:         logs.push(`Dòng ${i + 1}: Chuyển ${key} thành Mảng TOML (Array) chuẩn -> ${newArrVal}`);

449:         continue;
450:       }
451: 
452:       // Check if general string value needs quoting
453:       if (

455:         !val.startsWith('"') &&
456:         !val.startsWith("'") &&
457:         !val.startsWith('[') &&
458:         !val.startsWith('{') &&

463:         const isPureNumber = !isNaN(Number(val)) && !val.includes('..') && !/^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/.test(val);

465:         if (!isPureNumber) {

468:           fixCount++;
469:           logs.push(`Dòng ${i + 1}: Thêm dấu ngoặc kép cho ${key} = ${newVal}`);
470:         }

472: 
473:       // Escape unescaped backslashes inside already-quoted values (fixes "\\. invalid escape sequence")
474:       if (val.startsWith('"') && val.endsWith('"') && val.includes('\\')) {
475:         const safeVal = escapeBackslashes(val);

479:           logs.push(`Dòng ${i + 1}: Escape dấu gạch chéo ngược trong ${key} -> ${safeVal}`);
480:         }
481:       }
482:     }
483: 
484:     repairedLines.push(line);
485:   }
486: 
487:   return {

492: }

import os
import json

SERVER = "aquamc.vn"
SCRIPTS_DIR = "scripts"
BOTS_DIR = "bots"

# 1. Tạo thư mục scripts/ và bots/ nếu chưa có
os.makedirs(SCRIPTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(BOTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# 2. Định nghĩa nội dung các file .txt (script login MCC)
txt_files = {
    "login_khoablabla.txt": """wait 9
send /login khoalaptrinh
wait 2
send /server smp""",
    "login_ikujtyhfg.txt": """wait 9
send /login khoablabla
wait 2
send /server smp""",
    "login_afk.txt": """wait 9
send /login khoablabla
wait 2
send /server smp
wait 3
send /warp afk"""
}

# Tạo các file .txt trong thư mục scripts/
print("Đang tạo các file script trong thư mục scripts/...")
for filename, content in txt_files.items():
    filepath = os.path.join(SCRIPTS_DIR, filename)
    with open(filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(content.strip() + "\n")
    print(f"-> Đã tạo: {filepath}")

# 3. Danh sách bots (mỗi bot 1 thư mục riêng trong bots/)
accounts = [
    {"name": "khoablabla", "username": "khoablabla", "script": "login_khoablabla.txt"},
    {"name": "ikujtyhfg",  "username": "ikujtyhfg",  "script": "login_ikujtyhfg.txt"},
    {"name": "geasf",      "username": "geasf",      "script": "login_afk.txt"},
    {"name": "djaiwp",     "username": "djaiwp",     "script": "login_afk.txt"},
    {"name": "hdoiwa",     "username": "hdoiwa",     "script": "login_afk.txt"},
    {"name": "dnwauif",    "username": "dnwauif",    "script": "login_afk.txt"},
    {"name": "dhwaod",     "username": "dhwaod",     "script": "login_afk.txt"},
]

# Dọn dẹp file cũ thừa ở ngoài
os.system("rm -f run_*.sh script_*.txt login_*.txt")

print("\nĐang tạo cấu trúc bots/<tên_bot>/ ...")
for acc in accounts:
    name = acc["name"]
    bot_dir = os.path.join(BOTS_DIR, name)
    os.makedirs(bot_dir, exist_ok=True)

    # bot.json metadata (web UI đọc cái này)
    bot_json = {
        "id": name,
        "name": name,
        "username": acc["username"],
        "password": "-",
        "accountType": "mojang",
        "serverHost": SERVER,
        "serverPort": 25565,
        "minecraftVersion": "auto",
        "script": acc["script"],
    }
    with open(os.path.join(bot_dir, "bot.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(bot_json, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

    # run.sh - chạy MMC trực tiếp kèm script login
    sh_content = f"""#!/bin/bash
# Bot: {name} ({acc['username']} @ {SERVER}:25565)
# Script login: scripts/{acc['script']}
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
./MinecraftClient "{os.path.join(bot_dir, 'bot.ini')}" script="{os.path.join(SCRIPTS_DIR, acc['script'])}"
"""
    sh_filename = os.path.join(bot_dir, "run.sh")
    with open(sh_filename, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(sh_content)
    try:
        os.chmod(sh_filename, 0o755)
    except Exception:
        pass

    print(f"-> Đã tạo: {bot_dir}/ (bot.json + run.sh)")

print("\nHoàn tất! Các bot nằm gọn trong bots/<tên_bot>/, scripts trong scripts/.")
print("Mở web UI: tạo bot trong GUI sẽ tự tạo đủ các file. Script này tạo sẵn để khởi tạo nhanh.")

parts.text:
Now let me analyze MCC script format. MCC scripts: `wait` command takes milliseconds. So `wait 9` waits 9 ms — a real bug for login scripts (they should be `wait 9000`, `wait 2000`). Let me verify with the MCC docs... Actually MCC script syntax is:

```
# comment
wait 9000    # wait 9000 ms
send /help
```

So `wait 9` = 9ms and `wait 2` = 2ms — the scripts login too fast. That's a genuine bug (login scripts would send /login immediately).

Also there's a serious issue in createbot.py: `accountType: "mojang"` with `password: "-"`. In MCC, `AccountType = "mojang"` with password "-" means prompt for interactive login? Actually for offline mode MCC expects `AccountType = "mojang"` + password "-" works (offline). OK that's fine.

Now let me check the differences between MinecraftClient.ini (root) and bots/d/bot.ini to understand the state. The bot.ini is 619 lines; the root .ini 47KB. Let me diff root MinecraftClient.ini vs bots/d/bot.ini quickly, and check the working/backup.

Also key issues so far:

### CRITICAL
1. **Missing files `src/lib/mcVersions.ts` and `src/lib/savedAccounts.ts`** — imported by MCCConfigEditor.tsx (lines 33, 41-47) and MCCAccountSelector.tsx (lines 6, 7-13). These don't exist → frontend fails to compile → app won't run at all. (Also `.gitignore` has `lib/` which would ignore `src/lib/` — dangerous: any new file in src/lib won't be committed! `git check-ignore src/lib/iniHelper.ts` returned nothing though, so tracked files are fine. Wait, the output of git check-ignore was empty (no line printed for it) — hmm, actually the output only shows `git ls-files src/lib/` results. So iniHelper.ts is NOT ignored? `lib/` pattern in .gitignore — gitignore pattern `lib/` matches any directory named lib at any depth. But iniHelper.ts is tracked (already in index), so check-ignore on tracked files still reports them... Actually `git check-ignore` DOES report tracked files that match ignore patterns? No — git check-ignore reports paths that WOULD be ignored; tracked files are not ignored. Hmm, actually git check-ignore doesn't consider index status by default in older versions; in newer versions tracked files are excluded from the output unless --no-index. The empty output suggests it's not ignored... whatever. The real point: new files in src/lib might get accidentally ignored by `lib/` pattern if not already tracked. This explains why mcVersions.ts and savedAccounts.ts were never committed — they were probably created locally, gitignored, and this environment doesn't have them. So the app is broken.)

2. **Login scripts use wrong `wait` units** — MCC `wait` is milliseconds → `wait 9` = 9ms. Scripts should be `wait 9000`.

### Other bugs found

3. **`mccManager.ts:898-904` deleteAccount**: iterates clientState but only sends full state to clients whose activeAccountId === deleted id. Others get ACCOUNTS_LIST broadcast. OK. But **the deleted account's retryTimer is never cleared** — if a quick-exit retry timer is pending, `startMCC(targetId, true)` will fire on deleted account → inst undefined → returns. Minor leak.

4. **`stopMCC` race**: `proc.once('exit')` and `proc.once('close')` both call cleanupAndResolve — guarded by `resolved`. OK.

5. **`enableSilentMode`**: writes `MinTerminalWidth`/`Height` etc. Fine.

6. **Bug in `enableSilentMode`**: When `[ChatBot.AutoRelog]` exists but the `Enabled` line regex replacement fails (e.g. section exists but Enabled missing), the code doesn't add it — `/\[ChatBot.AutoRelog\][^\[]*/` test passes (section exists), then `replace` does nothing if no Enabled line. So "silent mode" may silently fail to disable AutoRelog. Same pattern in setAutoRelog? setAutoRelog has similar logic with a check `new RegExp(...).test(raw)` for already-set. For enableSilentMode, if section exists without Enabled, replace fails silently. Minor edge case.

7. **`parseIniToStatus` regex** — `raw.match(/Host\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/i)` — the first alternative matches ANY Host= inside the file, not necessarily the Server object; that's intended fallback. OK.

8. **`getStatusForAccount` running check**: `!!inst.mccProcess && !inst.mccProcess.killed`. If process exited but 'exit' handler not yet fired... fine.

9. **`server.ts` `/api/captcha-image` POST with colors**: `renderMapPaletteToPngBuffer(colors)` — client may send a JSON array; colors[?] fine. But if colors is a large Uint8Array via JSON, it's an array of numbers — OK.

10. **`mapRenderer.ts` palette**: BASE_MAP_PALETTE has only indices 0-35 (36 entries), but Minecraft map colors go to 63. `getMinecraftMapColor` uses `Math.floor(colorId/4)` → baseId up to 15 for colorId 63 → within 0..35. Wait, baseId = colorId/4 max = 15 (63/4=15.75→15). 36 entries cover baseId 0..35. So OK — colors 0..63 fully map. Fine.

11. **`iniHelper.serializeSectionsToIni`**: All string values get quoted. Comments? Values with `#` inside... minor.

12. **Critical: `handleSaveVisual` in MCCConfigEditor** serializes ONLY what's in the `sections` state — which came from `parseIniToSections(iniContent)`. parseIniToSections skips empty sections (settings.length === 0 && !description → skipped in serialize). **serializeSectionsToIni drops all comments and empty sections, and reorders** — saving visual config rewrites the whole ini, discarding comments and sections without settings. Since sections with 0 settings are dropped: sections like `[Main]` (no settings) dropped; `[Head]` has settings though. Also `# comment` lines get lost — including important comment headers. Worse: **all values get double-quoted** and the `# comment` text that was parsed gets re-appended. Data loss on save. This is a real bug (data-loss), but it's "by design" of visual editor maybe. Still worth flagging.

13. **`useBotWebSocket` LOG_MESSAGE slice**: `[...prev.slice(-999), message.log]` — keeps 1000. OK.

14. **`MCCMovementPanel` `/move` command**: MCC command is `/move <direction>` or `/move <x> <y> <z>`? MCC has `/move` with directions north/south/etc? Actually MCC movement: `/move <Direction>` where direction ∈ north, south, west, east, up, down, plus `/move <x> <y> <z>`. OK.

15. **`MCCMovementPanel` handleGoToCoords sends `/move ${nx} ${ny} ${nz}`** — fine.

16. **`MCCTerminal` history dedupe** — minor.

17. **`App.tsx` hasCaptchaAlert** uses `log.text` — for ansi logs text is plain text too. OK.

18. **`mccManager.addLog` 'kicked' type for normal process exit** — every exit logs as 'kicked' type. Cosmetic.

19. **BIG ONE — `updateServerAccount` password flow**: `inst.profile.password = creds.password` only when password defined. But `resolveCredentials` returns `password: '-'` when empty. Then syncProfileToIni writes `Password = "-"`. For mojang acc without password, MCC will prompt for login interactively — MCC in non-interactive mode fails? MCC prompts in console, and our spawn has stdin open so it can work. Minor.

20. **`server.ts` in production static** — fine.

21. **The `metadata.json` says Gemini capability but no Gemini usage** — not a bug per se.

22. **`vite.config.ts` watch ignore includes '**/MinecraftClient*.ini'** — ok.

23. **`MCCConfigEditor` imports `ini` parse from server... `parsedIni` prop unused** — it destructures `parsedIni` in App but MCCConfigEditor doesn't use it (`parsedIni` isn't even destructured in the component — right, it's not in destructured props. Fine.)

24. **Missing dependency on `ini` types for `ini.parse(content)`** — `@types/ini` in devDeps. OK.

25. **In `mccManager.init()` is async but constructor doesn't await** — `startMCC` calls `ensureBinaryAndIni()` first, and `loadAccounts` races. If a client connects and calls START_MCC before loadAccounts finishes, `instances` is empty → startMCC returns silently. And `addClient` on connect calls `sendFullStateToClient` — if accounts not yet loaded, sends empty ACCOUNTS_LIST and no INI. Then later loadAccounts completes but the client isn't re-notified! **The client would hang with no accounts until reconnect/refresh.** Race condition bug. Similarly the REST `/api/mcc/ini` may return empty initially. Worth flagging.

26. **`sendFullStateToClient` sends ACCOUNTS_LIST then logs etc. For the newly connected client** — it uses `this.activeAccountId`; but the client's `activeAccountId` state in `clientState` was set. OK.

27. **`broadcastStatus` when accountId undefined uses this.activeAccountId — fine.

28. **In `handleClientMessage`, `UPDATE_SERVER_ACCOUNT` → `updateServerAccount` is async but not awaited; errors unhandled → unhandled promise rejection?** updateServerAccount has try/catch? No — it does fs writes sync (saveAccountsToDisk uses sync fs inside try/catch). OK.

29. **`stopThenSaveIniAndRestart` calls `this.saveIniContent(raw, targetId)`** — that calls fixAndSanitizeIniContent. OK.

30. **`setAutoRelog` regex**: `raw.replace(/(\[ChatBot\.AutoRelog\][^\[]*?Enabled\s*=\s*)(true|false)/i, '$1${enabled}')` — replaced value is literal `${enabled}` string interpolation — WAIT. Look carefully:

```js
raw = raw.replace(/(\[ChatBot\.AutoRelog\][^\[]*?Enabled\s*=\s*)(true|false)/i, `$1${enabled}`);
```

The replacement string is `$1${enabled}` — template literal! `$1` followed by `${enabled}`. So replacement = "$1" + String(enabled) → correct, `$1` is the backreference. Good.

But enableSilentMode uses `'$1false'` similarly. OK.

Hmm wait, but there's a subtle bug: the regex `[^\[]*?` is non-greedy so it works.

31. **`enableSilentMode` bug**: if the section exists, `if (/\[ChatBot.AutoRelog\][^\[]*/.test(raw))` is true, but replace may not match (no Enabled line) → silently leaves AutoRelog enabled. Also **`enableSilentMode` never disables `[ChatBot.AntiAFK]`** — the main AFK kicker. And `ChatBot` list at top: MCC uses `ChatBot = [ "AutoRelog", "ScriptScheduler", "AutoRespond", "AutoEat", "AntiAFK" ]` in `[Main]` — disabling sections' Enabled might be insufficient if the bots aren't even registered. Also silent mode disables AutoRespond, but the anti-kick mechanism for AquaMC likely requires /afk command. Not code bugs per se, design.

32. **Real functional bug: `sendCommand` with commands while MCC running — input lines prefixed?** MCC interprets `/x` as MCC command and everything else as chat. So sending plain text sends chat. Good.

33. **`MCCMinimapRadar` posMatch regex identical to server's parseAndBroadcastCoords** — duplicated logic, fine.

34. **Position regex bug in `parseAndBroadcastCoords` r2**: `(?:position|location|coords|at)\D*...` matches "at" inside words? e.g. "Logout"... r1 first. Minor.

35. **CRITICAL-ish: `getAccountsSummaries` calls `getStatusForAccount(id)` which does `parseIniToStatus` (sync readFileSync) per account per broadcast — fine perf.

36. **`loadAccounts` uses `readdir` with withFileTypes; skips non-directories; but bot dirs could also be hidden etc. Fine.

37. **`deleteAccount` doesn't cancel retryTimer** (mentioned). Also doesn't delete logs. Fine.

38. **`startMCC` while `retryTimer` set: cleared. Good.

39. **`stopMCC` sets stoppedByUser = true — but if process already exited (mccProcess set to null), inst.mccProcess null → "No active process" and returns. OK.

40. **Process exit handler: after exit, `inst.mccProcess = null`. But `stopMCC`'s kill timer references `proc` var — safe.

41. **A REAL BUG in `startMCC` auto-relaunch logic**: `if (!isAutoRelaunch) inst.retryCount = 0;` — but on successful long uptime exit (>= 45s), retryCount reset in else branch. Fine. But note: comment says "< 30s" while constant is 45000. Cosmetic.

42. **`server.ts` POST /api/mcc/ini** — global save to active account; but client also has SAVE_INI via WS. Both exist. When user saves via config editor, it sends SAVE_INI through WS with accountId → saveIniContent does stop-then... no wait — `saveIniContent` does NOT stop MCC first! Only `setAutoRelog` and `enableSilentMode` use stopThenSaveIniAndRestart. **The main INI editor save (`SAVE_INI` → `saveIniContent`) writes bot.ini while MCC is running, and MCC rewrites bot.ini on exit → changes clobbered!** The comment in stopThenSaveIniAndRestart explains this exact problem ("MCC rewrites bot.ini from its in-memory config when it exits, so writing the INI before the stop gets clobbered"), but saveIniContent (used by the visual editor and raw editor — the main editing paths) does NOT stop/restart MCC. So **config changes made via the editor are lost when MCC exits**. That's a significant real bug — the workaround exists but is only wired into AutoRelog/SilentMode paths.

43. **`MCCConfigEditor` raw editor**: after save, `setRawText(serializedIni)` in visual mode sets rawText but sections update from WS INI_CONTENT broadcast. OK.

44. **`ini.parse(content)` in broadcastIniContent may throw** if INI has syntax errors that survive fixAndSanitize (e.g. unbalanced braces). `ini.parse` from npm 'ini' is tolerant. OK.

45. **Security: passwords stored in plaintext in bot.json + ini, served via REST /api/mcc/ini without auth** — no auth on any endpoint; the server binds 0.0.0.0. Anyone on the network can read passwords and control bots. Security issue worth flagging.

46. **`createbot.py` mismatch with actual repo bots/**: The repo has only bots/d (from git), created via UI presumably. accounts.json is stale (says acc-default but loadAccounts reads from bots/*/bot.json only; accounts.json is never used by code — actually is accounts.json read anywhere? grep: saveAccountsToDisk writes bot.json in bots dirs. accounts.json at root seems legacy unused. Let me grep quickly.

47. **`uniqueBotId` while loop condition**: `while (this.instances.has(id) || (fs.existsSync(pathModule.join(this.botsDir, id)) && id !== base))` — if id === base and dir exists (bot folder exists on disk but not in instances, e.g. created manually), it does NOT increment → collision with existing folder on disk! Because `id !== base` is false when id===base on first iteration. So adding a bot named same as an existing folder (but not loaded) overwrites. Edge case.

48. **`loadAccounts` and bot folders with invalid bot.json are skipped** but their folder remains; uniqueBotId can collide (as above).

49. **Chat log `type: 'kicked'` on every exit — used by MCCTerminal to color amber — every normal /quit shows "KICKED" styling. Cosmetic.

50. **In `MCCMapCaptchaPanel.handleTriggerSilentMode`** — fetch('/api/mcc/silent-mode') triggers silent mode for the active account on server — but wait, server's `mccManager.enableSilentMode()` uses `this.activeAccountId` (global), NOT the client's selected account! **The REST endpoints (`/api/mcc/silent-mode`, `/api/mcc/ini`) don't know which account the client selected** — they operate on the server-global activeAccountId, which is only updated by deleteAccount or initial load. If user has 2 bots and selects bot B in UI, then clicks "Silent Mode", it modifies bot A's ini (or fails if no account). REAL BUG. Also `/api/mcc/ini` GET/POST same issue. The WS protocol passes accountId correctly, but these REST endpoints don't. Since UI uses WS for INI (good) but REST for silent-mode (bug), silent mode may affect the wrong bot.

Also MCCMapCaptchaPanel fetches /api/mcc/silent-mode with no accountId param → always targets global activeAccountId → typically bot A, even if viewing bot B. Confirmed bug.

51. **`server.ts` serveCaptchaImage** — res.send(pngBuf) where pngBuf could be null? getCurrentCaptchaPngBuffer never returns null. OK.

52. **`handleUpdateServerPngCode` posts to /api/captcha-image with code; renderMapPaletteToPngBuffer not used for it. OK.

53. **Missing `send` fallback when WS not open: silent drop. Fine.

54. **`MCCAccountSelector` modal `createPortal` + `AnimatePresence` conditional — fine.

55. **`formData` password for offline reset to '-' — resolveAccountCredentials handles '-'. OK.

56. **`updateServerAccount` doesn't restart MCC or notify "will apply on restart"** — changes apply only after restart; UI doesn't say that. Minor UX.

57. **`server.ts` has no error handler for `/api/mcc/ini` POST when no account exists → saveIniContent returns false, but server returns `res.json({ success })` with success:false and no message. Fine.

58. **Race: two concurrent startMCC for same account** — guarded by running check but not atomic; two spawns possible if called within same tick? spawn is sync after await ensureBinaryAndIni — both would pass the check before the await? No: check happens before await; both calls could pass check simultaneously → double spawn. Minor.

59. **`ansiConverter` with `newline: true` and stream false — fine.

60. **`.env.example` mentions GEMINI_API_KEY but no code uses Gemini; @google/genai dependency unused. Not a bug.

61. **Big one for the actual AFK goal: MCC `AntiAFK` bot** — for AquaMC they may want `/afk` or AntiAFK bot enabled in template? template.ini ChatBot section — let me check what bots are configured in template.ini around line 300-608. Let me grep the ChatBot list and AntiAFK config in template.ini to see if it's set up for AFK (MoveInterval etc).

The `AntiAFK` bot has `Enabled = true` inside `[ChatBot.AntiAFK]`, but without `ChatBot = [ "AntiAFK" ]` in the `[ChatBot]` section, MCC will never instantiate the bot. This is critical for an AFK bot project: the bot would get kicked for AFK (well, actually AquaMC might kick for AFK — the whole point is to avoid that).

Actually wait — MCC's bot loading: In MCC config, `ChatBot` list in `[Main]` (or `[ChatBot]`) section: `ChatBot = [ "AntiAFK" ]`. The working.ini had `ChatBot = [ ]` (empty) at line 19 under `[Main]`... Actually looking at working.ini line 19: `ChatBot = [ ]` — under `[Main]` section presumably. So the working copy has ChatBot = [ ] (empty array) → no bots loaded.

The other files (root MinecraftClient.ini, template, bot.ini) don't even have the key → MCC default might load all bots with Enabled=true? No — MCC loads bots listed in ChatBot array; if the key is missing, default is... possibly empty (no bots). So AntiAFK is NOT active despite Enabled=true. This is a functional bug: the AFK protection doesn't actually work.

Hmm, actually I should double check MCC behavior: In MCC's config docs, the ChatBot array is under `[ChatBot]` section as `ChatBot = [ "Alerts", ... ]`. Default when missing... I believe missing means no bots. Since the entire template has `Enabled = true` for AntiAFK but no `ChatBot = [...]` list anywhere, the bots won't load. This is a bug worth flagging.

Also note `mccManager.enableSilentMode()` disables AutoRelog/ScriptScheduler/AutoRespond Enabled flags — but does NOT touch the `ChatBot = [...]` list. And the AutoRelog toggle in UI writes `[ChatBot.AutoRelog] Enabled = ...` — but again, if `ChatBot` list doesn't include "AutoRelog", this does nothing. The UI toggles have no effect if the ChatBot list is empty! That's a significant functional bug: `SET_AUTORELOG` and silent mode won't work because the bots aren't in the active list.

Now the missing modules — CRITICAL. Let me confirm what functions the missing files must export based on usage:

MCCAccountSelector.tsx uses:
- `MC_VERSIONS` from '../lib/mcVersions' (line 6)
- `loadSavedAccounts`, `saveSavedAccount`, `deleteSavedAccount`, `resolveAccountCredentials`, `SavedAccount` from '../lib/savedAccounts' (lines 7-13)

- `loadSavedAccounts`, `saveSavedAccount`, `deleteSavedAccount`, `resolveAccountCredentials`, `SavedAccount` from '../lib/savedAccounts' (lines 41-47)

So I need to create both files in the fix plan. Type signature from usage:
- `MC_VERSIONS: string[]`
- `SavedAccount` type: `{ id: string; username: string; password: string; accountType: 'offline' | 'mojang' | 'microsoft' | 'yggdrasil' }` roughly
- `loadSavedAccounts(): SavedAccount[]`
- `saveSavedAccount(acc: Omit<SavedAccount, 'id'>): SavedAccount[]` (returns the new full list)
- `deleteSavedAccount(id: string): SavedAccount[]`

4. **Login scripts `wait 9` should be `wait 9000`** — MCC wait takes ms. This causes login to happen instantly → "You are logging in too fast" kick. This is exactly the problem the backoff logic was written for! Fix: change to `wait 9000` etc.

5. **`mccManager` unused import `IniSection`? No. `MCCProcessStatus` etc fine. Unused imports `IniSection`... let me check: imports { MCCProcessStatus, ChatMessageLog, PlayerPosition, WSMessageFromServer, WSMessageFromClient, AccountProfile, AccountSummary } — all used? AccountSummary used in getAccountsSummaries. Yes.

MCC ini parser: keys without a section header default to... The current section. If appended at end of file after other sections like `[ChatBot.TelegramBridge]`, the `Account = ...` lines belong to the last section → INVALID config → MCC might fail to parse or ignore them! This is a REAL bug: `syncProfileToIni` appends to the end of the raw text without inserting into `[Main.General]`. Let me verify: in bots/d/bot.ini, where is the Account line? Line 12 — under `[Main.General]` (good, that came from template). But when user updates server account via `updateServerAccount` → `syncProfileToIni(inst.iniPath, inst.profile)`:

But for an AFK 24/7 bot, a kick after long uptime should also trigger relaunch... The MCC AutoRelog bot should handle it, but AutoRelog isn't in ChatBot list. Design decision, flag it.

15. **`server.ts` REST `/api/mcc/ini` GET/POST operate on global activeAccountId — NOT the client's selected account** (no accountId param). If client selects bot B, GET /api/mcc/ini (not used by UI though — UI uses WS) — silent-mode POST also uses global. **`/api/mcc/silent-mode` ignores client-selected account** — the captcha panel's "Bật Chế Độ Im Lặng" button affects the global active account, which is only set when a client selects... wait, `selectAccountForClient` updates per-client state, NOT the global `this.activeAccountId`. 24. **`MCCMapCaptchaPanel` POST /api/captcha-image with code — generates sample captcha (not the actual server map). This is a mock/demo. The actual map captcha from the server comes via MCC map packets which need `/map` command + rendering from console colors. The PNG server endpoint only shows sample digits, NOT the actual in-game map! So the "Giải Mã Map Captcha" feature is fake — it renders a sample image, not real map data. Flag: the captcha PNG never reflects the real server map; there's no mechanism to feed MCC map packet data into renderMapPaletteToPngBuffer (no WS message for map colors). REAL functional gap.

25. **`mapRenderer` `colors` param type `number[] | Uint8Array`** — `colors[idx]` fine.

26. **`useBotWebSocket` `scripts` state typed `string[]`** but server returns array of `{name, content}` objects; `setScripts(data.scripts)` assigns objects into `string[]` typed state. TS error (missing types) — actually with `any` from res.json(), no compile error but runtime `scripts.map((s) => s.name)` works. Type mismatch only.

But critically it DROPS sections with 0 settings and ALL comments + description lines, and **reorders** everything. Save Visual rewrites whole INI losing structure/comments. Also number `1.0` → `1`? 36. **vite.config.ts comment contains mojibake `â`** cosmetic.

37. **`index.css`** — let me quickly check it for tailwind import. Not critical.

38. **`startMCC` spawn env TERM** fine.

39. **`enableSilentMode` also sets AutoRespond off — but on next MCC exit MCC rewrites bot.ini from in-memory config** — the stopThenSaveIniAndRestart handles the ordering (stop → wait → save → start). OK.

40. **AutoRelog `Enabled` written with `$1${enabled}`** — replacement `$1` + 'true'. OK.

41. **`setAutoRelog` already-set check**: if Enabled=true already and enabling again — no-op fine.

42. **`readAutoRelogFromIni`** parses `[ChatBot.AutoRelog]` section Enabled — OK.

43. **`getStatusForAccount` username: `inst.profile.username || parsed.username`** OK.

44. **`parseIniToStatus` `AccountType` fallback** OK.

45. **`updateServerAccount` doesn't update `minecraftVersion` when empty string passed → keep old. OK.

46. **Potential unhandled rejection**: `handleClientMessage` calls async methods without catch — `this.addAccount(msg.profile).then(...)` — if addAccount throws (e.g., fs error), unhandled rejection. Minor.

47. **`uniqueBotId` while loop**: `fs.existsSync(botDir) && id !== base` — if id === base and folder exists on disk (from createbot.py) but not in instances, it would skip incrementing because `id !== base` false → returns `base` even though folder exists → overwrites existing bot folder data! Wait: condition to CONTINUE loop is `instances.has(id) || (exists && id !== base)`. If base folder exists but no instance: instances.has false; exists true but id===base → false → loop ends, returns base → later `fs.mkdirSync` (exists_ok) and `fs.writeFileSync(iniPath, baseIni)` — overwrites the existing bot's bot.ini! But wait — loadAccounts loads all bot folders with valid bot.json into instances first (init before any addAccount), so instances.has(base) would be true for those. Only un-loaded folders (broken bot.json) can be overwritten. Minor edge.

Fix: gate or emit after load.

51. **`enableSilentMode` in server REST** — same global-account bug as #15.

52. **login script: `send /login khoalaptrinh` — the password is in plaintext txt files served over HTTP without auth** (already noted).

53. **`MCCConfigEditor` `quickType` default 'offline'** — initial form shows offline even if server account is mojang; handleApplyQuickAccount uses resolveAccountCredentials('offline', '-') → accountType 'mojang', password '-'. OK.

54. **`handleApplyQuickAccount`** — `if (validPort !== quickPort) setQuickPort(validPort);` — quickPort typed number; if NaN, validPort 25565. OK.

55. **In `MCCConfigEditor` visual save: `serializeSectionsToIni` DROPS `[Head]`? It has settings so kept. But **`[ChatBot]` section with 0 settings dropped** — meaning the `ChatBot = [...]` list would be dropped if it existed. Since it doesn't exist in files anyway.

Hmm wait, actually let me double-check MCC docs: the ChatBot list key IS `ChatBot = [ ... ]` in section `[ChatBot]`. Since all INI files lack it, no bots load. But actually — MCC may auto-load bots whose sections have `Enabled = true`? No. MCC requires the ChatBot array. Let me verify from MCC docs quickly... I recall MCC config: `ChatBot = [ "Alerts", "AntiAFK", "AutoRelog", ... ]` under `[ChatBot]`. Yes. So missing → no bots. The AutoRelog toggle, silent mode etc. all no-op. And the bot gets kicked for AFK after X minutes (the reason this project exists!).

Wait, but bots/d/bot.ini line 223 `[ChatBot.AntiAFK] Enabled = true` — and there IS no ChatBot list. Hmm, but maybe MCC auto-enables bots with Enabled=true if the list is absent? I'm fairly confident MCC only loads bots in the list. I'll flag it as "verify/fix: add ChatBot = [...] list".

Let me quickly verify MCC's actual behavior with a web search later; for the plan I'll include it as a probable bug requiring the ChatBot list.

Also **`matches.ini`** is just `[AutoRespond]` — AutoRespond disabled anyway.

**`MinecraftClient` binary is 88MB committed to git** — flagged but fine.

**`.gitignore` includes `lib/`** — this is why src/lib/mcVersions.ts & savedAccounts.ts can't be committed! Pattern `lib/` matches any directory named `lib` at any level... Actually gitignore patterns without leading slash match at any level: `lib/` matches `src/lib/`! So git would ignore new files in src/lib — explaining why these files are missing from the repo even if created locally. The fix: change `lib/` to `/lib/` and `libs/` to `/libs/` etc., or use `!src/lib/`. This is an important root-cause finding!

parts.text:
CONFIRMED root cause: `.gitignore` line 14 `lib/` matches `src/lib/` — any new file in `src/lib/` is ignored by git, which is exactly why `mcVersions.ts` and `savedAccounts.ts` never made it into the repo and don't exist in this checkout. The app is broken until those files are restored.

Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me also quickly double check MCC `wait` units for scripts to be sure about the bug. MCC script: `wait <milliseconds>`. From MCC docs: `wait 1000` waits 1000ms. So `wait 9` = 9ms. Yes, bug.

Also check `matches.ini` — just `[AutoRespond]`, matches file for AutoRespond. fine.

Let me also verify the AutoRelog toggle regex replacement uses `$1` + boolean, that's fine.

One more check on the `handleClientMessage` `UPDATE_ACCOUNT` — when profile has only `script`, it's handled. When updating password only, skip. fine.

Also confirm the "Silent Mode" REST endpoint global-account bug. Yes: `app.post('/api/mcc/silent-mode')` → `mccManager.enableSilentMode()` → `targetId = accountId || this.activeAccountId` — accountId undefined → uses global `this.activeAccountId` which only changes on deleteAccount/init. Client-selected account (per-client state) is ignored. Bug confirmed.

Similarly REST `/api/mcc/ini` GET/POST — but UI doesn't use those (uses WS SAVE_INI which correctly passes accountId). Only silent-mode REST used by UI → wrong bot targeted.

Now compile the final plan. The user's request: "đọc toàn bộ dự án và tìm ra lỗi" (read the entire project and find the errors). "quet sau" = "scan later" — probably means scan the rest later, or it's a typo. I'll present a comprehensive bug report with a fix plan.

Let me organize the findings by severity:

## CRITICAL (app won't run / data loss)
1. **Missing files `src/lib/mcVersions.ts` and `src/lib/savedAccounts.ts`** — imported by MCCAccountSelector.tsx:6-13 & MCCConfigEditor.tsx:33,41-47. Cause: `.gitignore:14` pattern `lib/` ignores `src/lib/` → files never committed. Fix: restore both files + fix .gitignore (`/libs/`, `/lib/`, `/libraries/` with leading slashes or `!src/lib/`).
2. **Login scripts `wait 9` / `wait 2` / `wait 3`** — MCC `wait` unit is milliseconds → waits 9ms/2ms/3ms instead of 9s/2s/3s. Causes "logging in too fast" kicks (the exact problem the code comments mention). Fix to `wait 9000` etc.
3. **`ChatBot = [...]` list missing in every INI** (template, bots/*/bot.ini, root ini) — MCC only loads bots listed there; `[ChatBot.AntiAFK] Enabled = true` is a no-op without it. Also makes AutoRelog toggle & Silent Mode ineffective (they only flip `Enabled` flags). Verify against MCC behavior; likely fix: add `ChatBot = [ "AntiAFK", ... ]` under `[ChatBot]`.

## HIGH (functional bugs)
4. **Editor saves get clobbered by MCC on exit** — `saveIniContent` (used by SAVE_INI from config editor) writes bot.ini while MCC runs; MCC rewrites bot.ini from in-memory config on exit (the code comments acknowledge this, and stopThenSaveIniAndRestart exists but is only used by AutoRelog/SilentMode). Config editor changes are lost. Fix: use stopThenSaveIniAndRestart path for SAVE_INI too.
5. **REST endpoints use global active account** — `/api/mcc/silent-mode` (used by Captcha panel) targets `this.activeAccountId` (server-global), not the client's selected account; with 2+ bots the wrong bot is modified. Also `/api/mcc/ini` GET/POST. Fix: accept accountId param / route via WS.
6. **Startup race** — `mccManager` constructor fires async `init()`; clients connecting before `loadAccounts()` finishes get empty ACCOUNTS_LIST and are never re-notified (no accounts visible until refresh; REST INI empty). Fix: await init before listen / broadcast after load.
7. **Captcha PNG is fake** — `/captcha.png` renders sample digits, never real in-game map data; there's no pipeline feeding MCC map packet colors into `renderMapPaletteToPngBuffer`. The map captcha feature cannot actually solve AquaMC captchas. 
8. **`.gitignore` `lib/` also risks future loss** (root cause of #1).

## MEDIUM
9. `enableSilentMode` regex replace silently fails when section exists without `Enabled` key.
10. No auto-relaunch after long-uptime kicks (only <45s exits) — for 24/7 AFK purpose, kicked-after-hours bots never come back (AutoRelog bot not enabled). 
11. `syncProfileToIni` appends new keys at file end (outside `[Main.General]`) when keys are absent → invalid section placement.
12. `deleteAccount` doesn't clear pending `retryTimer`.
13. Security: no auth on any endpoint; login passwords in scripts/*.txt exposed via `/api/scripts`; plaintext passwords; server binds 0.0.0.0.
14. `serializeSectionsToIni` (Visual editor save) drops all comments, empty sections, and rewrites whole file → comment loss.
15. `createbot.py` scripts also have `wait 9` bug + accountType mojang with password "-" (offline actually works but mojang type + "-" prompts for interactive login → stuck at login prompt).
16. TS: `scripts` state typed `string[]` but holds objects; minor.
17. Unhandled async rejections in handleClientMessage (addAccount etc.).
18. `handleScanCoords` sends `/whereami` (not an MCC command).

Also worth mentioning: unused deps (mineflayer, three, socks-proxy-agent, @google/genai), accounts.json legacy unused, 88MB binary in git.

Now present the plan concisely. The user is in plan mode. I should present findings + proposed fixes, and ask if they want me to fix them all or prioritize. Keep it organized. Vietnamese response.

Đã đọc xong toàn bộ dự án. Dưới đây là kết quả quét (scan) lỗi, xếp theo mức độ nghiêm trọng:

## 🔴 CRITICAL — App không chạy được

**1. Thiếu 2 file `src/lib/mcVersions.ts` và `src/lib/savedAccounts.ts`**
- `MCCAccountSelector.tsx:6-13` và `MCCConfigEditor.tsx:33,41-47` import chúng, nhưng file không tồn tại → build/lint fail, app không khởi động được.
- **Nguyên nhân gốc**: `.gitignore:14` có pattern `lib/` — khớp với mọi thư mục tên `lib` ở bất kỳ cấp nào, kể cả `src/lib/` (đã xác minh: `git check-ignore -v src/lib/mcVersions.ts` trả về `.gitignore:14:lib/`). Nên 2 file này chưa bao giờ được commit.
- → Cần tạo lại 2 file + sửa `.gitignore` (thêm gạch đầu `/lib/` hoặc `!src/lib/`).

**2. Script login dùng sai đơn vị `wait`**
- `scripts/login_*.txt`: `wait 9`, `wait 2`, `wait 3` — MCC tính `wait` bằng **milli giây** → chỉ chờ 9ms/2ms/3ms thay vì 9s/2s/3s. Bot gửi `/login` ngay khi chưa join xong → bị AquaMC kick "logging in too fast" (đúng lỗi mà code backoff ở mccManager.ts:41-45 cố xử lý).
- → Sửa thành `wait 9000`, `wait 2000`, `wait 3000`.

**3. Không có danh sách `ChatBot = [...]` trong mọi file INI**
- `template.ini`, `bots/d/bot.ini`, `MinecraftClient.ini` đều **không có key `ChatBot = [ "AntiAFK", ... ]`** trong section `[ChatBot]` (chỉ có `MinecraftClient.working.ini` với `ChatBot = [ ]` rỗng).
- MCC chỉ load các bot nằm trong danh sách này → `[ChatBot.AntiAFK] Enabled = true` **không có tác dụng**; bot vẫn bị kick AFK. Kéo theo lỗi #4 và #5 (AutoRelog/Silent Mode bật `Enabled` nhưng bot không được load).

## 🟠 HIGH — Lỗi chức năng nghiêm trọng

**4. Sửa INI trong editor bị mất khi MCC thoát**
- `saveIniContent` (SAVE_INI từ config editor) ghi `bot.ini` trong khi MCC đang chạy — nhưng MCC **tự ghi đè bot.ini từ config trong bộ nhớ khi thoát** (chính comment ở mccManager.ts:690-692 thừa nhận điều này). Hàm `stopThenSaveIniAndRestart` đã có sẵn nhưng **chỉ được dùng** bởi AutoRelog/Silent Mode, không dùng cho đường SAVE_INI chính → mọi thay đổi cấu hình đều bị mất.

**5. REST endpoints dùng account toàn cục, không phải account client đang chọn**
- `/api/mcc/silent-mode` (nút "Bật Chế Độ Im Lặng" trong tab Captcha) gọi `mccManager.enableSilentMode()` → dùng `this.activeAccountId` (global), **không phải** account mà client đang chọn. Có 2+ bot là sửa nhầm bot khác. `/api/mcc/ini` GET/POST cũng cùng vấn đề.

**6. Race condition lúc khởi động**
- Constructor `mccManager` gọi `init()` async không await (mccManager.ts:57-59). Client WS kết nối trước khi `loadAccounts()` xong sẽ nhận `ACCOUNTS_LIST` rỗng và **không bao giờ được gửi lại** → UI hiện 0 bot tới khi refresh.

**7. Tab "Giải Mã Map Captcha" là giả**
- `/captcha.png` và `/api/captcha-image` chỉ render **mã mẫu do người dùng nhập** (`generateSampleCaptchaPngBuffer`), không có pipeline nào đưa dữ liệu map packet thật của server vào `renderMapPaletteToPngBuffer` → không thể giải captcha thật được.

**8. Kicked sau thời gian dài online (>45s) thì không tự relaunch**
- mccManager.ts:598-616 chỉ auto-relaunch khi uptime < 45s. Bot bị kick lúc 2h sáng sẽ chết vĩnh viễn (và AutoRelog bot lại chưa được load — lỗi #3).

## 🟡 MEDIUM — Lỗi khác

9. `enableSilentMode`/`setAutoRelog`: section tồn tại nhưng thiếu dòng `Enabled` → `replace()` không khớp, lặng lẽ thất bại.
10. `syncProfileToIni` (mccManager.ts:258-301): khi key chưa có, **append vào cuối file** ngoài `[Main.General]` → key rơi vào section sai → MCC đọc sai.
11. `deleteAccount` không clear `retryTimer` đang chờ → timer vẫn fire nhưng account đã xóa.
12. `serializeSectionsToIni` (Visual editor save) **mất toàn bộ comment**, section rỗng, và viết lại cả file.
13. Bảo mật: không có auth trên mọi endpoint, server bind `0.0.0.0`; **mật khẩu login nằm trong `scripts/*.txt` lộ qua `/api/scripts`**; password plaintext trong `bot.json`.
14. `createbot.py`: cùng lỗi `wait 9`; tạo `accountType: "mojang"` với password `"-"` → MCC chờ nhập login tương tác.
15. `useBotWebSocket.ts:17`: state `scripts` khai báo `string[]` nhưng nhận object `{name, content}` (TS sai type).
16. `handleScanCoords` gửi `/whereami` — không phải lệnh MCC.

## ✅ Còn ổn (chỉ ghi chú)
- Dependencies thừa: `mineflayer`, `three`, `socks-proxy-agent`, `@google/genai` không được dùng.
- `accounts.json` ở root là legacy, code không đọc.
- Binary `MinecraftClient` 88MB đã commit vào git.

---

Bạn muốn tôi tiến hành sửa theo thứ tự nào? Gợi ý: sửa trước 3 lỗi CRITICAL (#1-3) để app chạy được, rồi tới HIGH (#4-8), còn MEDIUM tùy bạn chọn. Hoặc tôi có thể làm toàn bộ luôn.

 # Documentation: https://mccteam.github.io/g/bots/#discord-bridge
 # Setup:
 # First you need to create a Bot on the Discord Developers Portal, here is a video tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2FgMnZViNPA .
 # /!\ IMPORTANT /!\: When creating a bot, you MUST ENABLE "Message Content Intent", "Server Members Intent" and "Presence Intent" in order for bot to work! Also follow along carefully do not miss any steps!
 # When making a bot, copy the generated token and paste it here in "Token" field (tokens are important, keep them safe).
 # Copy the "Application ID" and go to: https://discordapi.com/permissions.html .
 # Paste the id you have copied and check the "Administrator" field in permissions, then click on the link at the bottom.
 # This will open an invitation menu with your servers, choose the server you want to invite the bot on and invite him.
 # Once you've invited the bot, go to your Discord client and go to Settings -> Advanced and Enable "Developer Mode".
 # Exit the settings and right click on a server you have invited the bot to in the server list, then click "Copy ID", and paste the id here in "GuildId".
 # Then right click on a channel where you want to interact with the bot and again right click -> "Copy ID", pase the copied id here in "ChannelId".
 # And for the end, send a message in the channel, right click on your nick and again right click -> "Copy ID", then paste the id here in "OwnersIds".
 # How to use:
 # To execute an MCC command, prefix it with a dot ".", example: ".move 143 64 735" .
 # To send a message, simply type it out and hit enter.
 [ChatBot.DiscordBridge]
 Enabled = false
 Token = "your bot token here"               # Your Discord Bot token.

 ChannelId = 1018565295654326364             # The ID of a channel where you want to interact with the MCC using the bot.

When set to a value like 1.0, messages received within that interval are batched into a single Discord message. Useful for reducing Discord API rate limits.
 # Message formats

 # This bot allows you to send and receive messages and commands via a Telegram Bot DM or to receive messages in a Telegram channel.
 # /!\ NOTE: You can't send messages and commands from a group channel, you can only send them in the bot DM, but you can get the messages from the client in a group channel.
 # -----------------------------------------------------------
 # Setup:
 # First you need to create a Telegram bot and obtain an API key, to do so, go to Telegram and find @botfather
 # Click on "Start" button and read the bot reply, then type "/newbot", the Botfather will guide you through the bot creation.
 # Once you create the bot, copy the API key that you have gotten, and put it into the "Token" field of "ChatBot.TelegramBridge" section (this section).
 # /!\ Do not share this token with anyone else as it will give them the control over your bot. Save it securely.
 # Then launch the client and go to Telegram, find your newly created bot by searching for it with its username, and open a DM with it.
 # Click on "Start" button and type and send the following command ".chatid" to obtain the chat id. 
 # Copy the chat id number (eg. 2627844670) and paste it in the "ChannelId" field and add it to the "Authorized_Chat_Ids" field (in this section) (an id in "Authorized_Chat_Ids" field is a number/long, not a string!), then save the file.
 # Now you can use the bot using it's DM.
 # /!\ If you do not add the id of your chat DM with the bot to the "Authorized_Chat_Ids" field, ayone who finds your bot via search will be able to execute commands and send messages!
 # /!\ An id pasted in to the "Authorized_Chat_Ids" should be a number/long, not a string!
 # -----------------------------------------------------------
 # NOTE: If you want to recieve messages to a group channel instead, make the channel temporarely public, invite the bot to it and make it an administrator, then set the channel to private if you want.
 # Then set the "ChannelId" field to the @ of your channel (you must include the @ in the settings, eg. "@mysupersecretchannel"), this is the username you can see in the invite link of the channel.
 # /!\ Only include the username with @ prefix, do not include the rest of the link. Example if you have "https://t.me/mysupersecretchannel", the "ChannelId" will be "@mysupersecretchannel".
 # /!\ Note that you will not be able to send messages to the client from a group channel!
 # -----------------------------------------------------------
 # How to use the bot:
 # To execute an MCC command, prefix it with a dot ".", example: ".move 143 64 735" .
 # To send a message, simply type it out and hit enter.
 [ChatBot.TelegramBridge]
 Enabled = false
 Token = "your bot token here"               # Your Telegram Bot token.
 ChannelId = ""                              # An ID of a channel where you want to interact with the MCC using the bot.
 Authorized_Chat_Ids = [ ]                   # A list of Chat IDs that are allowed to send messages and execute commands. To get an id of your chat DM with the bot use ".chatid" bot command in Telegram.
 Message_Send_Timeout = 3                    # How long to wait (in seconds) if a message can not be sent to Telegram before canceling the task (minimum 1 second).
 # Message formats
 # Words wrapped with { and } are going to be replaced during the code execution, do not change them!
 # For example. {message} is going to be replace with an actual message, {username} will be replaced with an username, {timestamp} with the current time.
 # For Telegram message formatting, check the following: https://mccteam.github.io/r/tg-fmt.html
 PrivateMessageFormat = "*(Private Message)* {username}: {message}"
 PublicMessageFormat = "{username}: {message}"
 TeleportRequestMessageFormat = "A new Teleport Request from **{username}**!"
 
 # A Chat Bot that collects items on the ground

 Enabled = false
 Collect_All_Item_Types = true               # If set to true, the bot will collect all items, regardless of their type. If you want to use the whitelisted item types, disable this by setting it to false
 Items_Whitelist = [ "Diamond", "NetheriteIngot", ] # In this list you can specify which items the bot will collect. To enable this, set the Collect_All_Item_Types to false. (NOTE: This does not prevent the bot from accidentally picking up other items, it only goes to positions where it finds the whitelisted items)\nYou can see the list of item types here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCCTeam/Minecraft-Console-Client/master/MinecraftClient/Inventory/ItemType.cs
 Delay_Between_Tasks = 300                   # Delay in milliseconds between bot scanning items (Recommended: 300-500)
 Collection_Radius = 30.0                    # The radius in which bot will look for items to collect (Default: 30)
 Always_Return_To_Start = true               # If set to true, the bot will return to it's starting position after there are no items to collect

 # This bot allows you to send and recieve messages and commands via a Discord channel.
 # For Setup you can either use the documentation or read here (Documentation has images).
 # Documentation: https://mccteam.github.io/g/bots/#discord-bridge
 # Setup:
 # First you need to create a Bot on the Discord Developers Portal, here is a video tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2FgMnZViNPA .
 # /!\ IMPORTANT /!\: When creating a bot, you MUST ENABLE "Message Content Intent", "Server Members Intent" and "Presence Intent" in order for bot to work! Also follow along carefully do not miss any steps!
 # When making a bot, copy the generated token and paste it here in "Token" field (tokens are important, keep them safe).
 # Copy the "Application ID" and go to: https://discordapi.com/permissions.html .
 # Paste the id you have copied and check the "Administrator" field in permissions, then click on the link at the bottom.
 # This will open an invitation menu with your servers, choose the server you want to invite the bot on and invite him.
 # Once you've invited the bot, go to your Discord client and go to Settings -> Advanced and Enable "Developer Mode".
 # Exit the settings and right click on a server you have invited the bot to in the server list, then click "Copy ID", and paste the id here in "GuildId".
 # Then right click on a channel where you want to interact with the bot and again right click -> "Copy ID", pase the copied id here in "ChannelId".
 # And for the end, send a message in the channel, right click on your nick and again right click -> "Copy ID", then paste the id here in "OwnersIds".
 # How to use:
 # To execute an MCC command, prefix it with a dot ".", example: ".move 143 64 735" .
 # To send a message, simply type it out and hit enter.
 [ChatBot.DiscordBridge]
 Enabled = false
 Token = "your bot token here"               # Your Discord Bot token.
 GuildId = 1018553894831403028               # The ID of a server/guild where you have invited the bot to.
 ChannelId = 1018565295654326364             # The ID of a channel where you want to interact with the MCC using the bot.
 OwnersIds = [ 978757810781323276, ]         # A list of IDs of people you want to be able to interact with the MCC using the bot.
 Message_Send_Timeout = 3                    # How long to wait (in seconds) if a message can not be sent to discord before canceling the task (minimum 1 second).
 Allow_Other_Bot_Messages = false            # When enabled, messages from other Discord bots in the channel will be relayed to Minecraft chat. The bridge always ignores its own messages to prevent loops.
 Relay_All_Messages = false                  # When enabled, all text received from the Minecraft server (including system messages, join/leave notifications, etc.) will be relayed to Discord, not just player chat and private messages.
 Message_Aggregation_Interval = 3.0          # Interval in seconds to aggregate messages before sending them to Discord. When set to 0, messages are sent immediately one by one. When set to a value like 1.0, messages received within that interval are batched into a single Discord message. Useful for reducing Discord API rate limits.
 # Message formats

The `setSectionEnabled` regex: `\[ChatBot\.ScriptScheduler\][^\[]*` — the `[^\[]*` stops at the next `[` which is the nested section header `[[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler.TaskList]]` right after `Enabled = false`. 

Looking at the original file, the ScriptScheduler section is:
```
[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler]
# comment lines
Enabled = false
TaskList...
[[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler.TaskList]]
```

The section match `[^\[]*` grabbed everything up to `[[...`, which includes `Enabled = false` but ALSO the `Task_Name` lines etc? In this case enabledRe `/^\s*Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)\s*$/im` should match just `Enabled = false` line... The `im` flag: `^` matches line start within the section string. `\s*` at start can match newlines. The regex `^\s*Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)\s*$` with multiline should match ONLY the `Enabled = false` line if it's alone on a line. But it matched `Enabled = "false[[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler.TaskList]]"` — that means the section text ended before `Enabled = false`... 

Wait, look: the replacement result is `Enabled = "false[[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler.TaskList]]"`. So `enabledRe` matched something spanning: `\s*Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)\s*` where `$` matched before `[`? With `m` flag, `$` matches before `\n` AND at end... but here the match seems to be: `...\nEnabled = false` then `$` matched at end-of-string? No — the section regex `[^\[]*` stops at the first `[`. If the section content is:

```
[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler]
Enabled = false
[[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler.TaskList]]
```

then section match = `[ChatBot.ScriptScheduler]\nEnabled = false\n`. The enabledRe = `/^\s*Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)\s*$/im` — with `m` flag, `\s*$`... wait `\s*` includes newlines! So `\s*$` can match... hmm no, `$` in multiline matches before `\n`. `^\s*Enabled...\s*$` — this could match `Enabled = false\n` where `\s*` swallows the trailing newline and `$` matches at end of string too. So it matches `Enabled = false\n` and replaces with `Enabled = ${enabled}` — dropping the newline. Result: `Enabled = false[[ChatBot...` — the newline got consumed by `\s*$`. That's the bug: `\s*$` consumed the `\n` before `[[`, then replacement string `Enabled = false` glued to `[[`.

Fix: make the enabled line regex anchor properly: `/^(\s*)Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)(\s*)$/im` and capture. Simpler: use `/^(?!.*=)[^\n]*/`... Let me write it robustly:

Replace with:
```ts
const enabledRe = /^(\s*Enabled\s*=\s*)(true|false)(\s*)$/im;
if (enabledRe.test(section)) {

```

Preserving the trailing `\s*` (the newline) as `$3`. `$2` replaced with `false`/`true`.

Wait but there's still an issue: the section content in `section` variable — `\s*` with `m`... `^(\s*Enabled...` — `^` matches at start of the `Enabled` line since multiline. Good. `(\s*)$` captures trailing whitespace including the newline. Replacement keeps it.

But another subtlety: for sections where `Enabled` is NOT the last line before the next `[`... e.g.:
```
[ChatBot.AutoRelog]
Enabled = true
Delay = ...
Retries = -1

[Next]
```

With multiline, `$` matches before each `\n`. `(\s*)$` after `true` → `\s*` matches empty, then `$` before `\n`. Match is just `Enabled = true` (no trailing newline consumed since `\s*` is greedy but `$` must follow — `\s*` greedy tries `\nDelay...` but then `$` needs to match after — fails. Backtrack: `\s*` = `` empty, `$` matches before `\n` at end of `Enabled = true`. So match = `Enabled = true`. Replacement `$1${enabled}` = `Enabled = false`. 

Hmm wait — `$` in JavaScript multiline matches BEFORE a `\n` at the end of a line segment. With `\s*$` — after `true`, `\s*` could match `\n` and continue to `Delay = ...`? `\s` = space\t\n\r\f\v — yes newlines are \s. So `\s*` is greedy and tries to consume `\nDelay = 1\n`... then `$` needs to match at end of string or before newline. Multi-line `$` can match at any position before `\n`. After consuming `\nDelay = 1`, the next char is `\n` and `$` CAN match there (before that newline). So `\s*` consumes `\nDelay = 1` and `$` matches before the following `\n`! The whole match = `\nDelay = 1` INCLUDING "Delay = 1" text?? No wait — `^\s*Enabled` — `^` must be at a line start, then `\s*` then literal `Enabled`. So the match starts at `Enabled`. Then `\s*` after `true`: greedy: `\nDelay = 1\n...`. `$` can match before any `\n`. So match extends from `Enabled` to before some `\n` consuming `\nDelay = 1` potentially. Then replacement would DELETE the Delay lines! Dangerous.

To avoid that, use a non-greedy `\s*?` with `$`: `/^(\s*)Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)(\s*?)$/im`. Lazy — try smallest first: empty `\s*`, `$` matches before `\n` right after `true`. If `Enabled = true` is at end of section string (no trailing \n), `$` matches end of string.

Also need to escape in replacement: use `$1` groups + literal newline terminator. 

Actually simpler and safer: operate line-wise. Rewrite setSectionEnabled to split section into lines and find the `Enabled = ...` line:

```ts
private setSectionEnabled(raw: string, sectionName: string, enabled: boolean): string {
  const escaped = sectionName.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
  const sectionRe = new RegExp(`\\[${escaped}\\][^\\[]*`, 'i');
  const sectionMatch = raw.match(sectionRe);
  if (!sectionMatch) {
    return `${raw.replace(/\n*$/, '')}\n\n[${sectionName}]\nEnabled = ${enabled}\n`;
  }
  const section = sectionMatch[0];
  const enabledLineRe = /^(\s*)Enabled\s*=\s*(true|false)\s*$/im;
  const enabledLineMatch = section.match(enabledLineRe);
  if (enabledLineMatch) {
    // replace only that exact line, keep everything else untouched
    const newSection = section.replace(enabledLineRe, `$1Enabled = ${enabled}`);
    return raw.replace(section, newSection);
  }
  // section exists but no Enabled line -> append
  const trimmed = section.replace(/\n+$/, '');
  return raw.replace(section, trimmed + (trimmed.endsWith('\n') || trimmed === '' ? '' : '\n') + `Enabled = ${enabled}\n`);
}
```

That still produces a valid replacement (capturing group includes the `\n`?? `$1` = `  \n` — replacement `$1Enabled = false` → `  \nEnabled = false` — newline inserted — WRONG).
